title: Representing Illegal States via Optional Fields (Primitive Obsession)
pattern: Multi-option structs where multiple interdependent fields are marked optional (`Option<T>`), but business logic requires exactly one to be present.
why_bad: Downstream code must include redundant assertions or fallback error-handling blocks, inflating complexity and risking runtime bugs.
detection: Struct definitions with multiple optional fields that represent mutually exclusive choices.
fix:
Refactor the optional fields into a typed enum with associated data, making illegal states unrepresentable.
```rust
enum PaymentMethod {
    Card { card_number: String },
    PayPal { email: String },
}
```
